facts.why: Spring and Crosby are real SoHo streets and the film is set in downtown Manhattan. The coffee shop is the menu's own venue and does not claim to be the film's diner.

facts.text: the Reverend's shelter on the Bowery
facts.why: Wikipedia says the Reverend runs the local homeless shelter but gives no street. Bowery is not shown anywhere, so it is dropped.
facts.fix: the Reverend's shelter, ready for dunking into the stew

facts.text: Greenwich Village cider doughnuts -- the Village above the sewers
facts.why: Nothing I opened puts the film in Greenwich Village, and the card sets the shop in SoHo. The film is set in New York over the sewers, so the name now says Manhattan.
facts.fix: Manhattan cider doughnuts -- the streets above the sewers

vibe.verdict: A coffee shop with a sewer map is a clever idea and looks great, but the film's best bits are barely used.
